name: Liberty Bell 7
type_description: Clock-syncable LFO, 16 waveforms, uni/bipolar mode, wave distortion
bom_parts_summary: ICs TL072, TL074, TAPLFO3; BC547 transistor; 1N4148 diodes; multiple rotary/SPST/SPDT switches
components_evidence: BOM lists part values/types only (e.g. BC547, TL072, TL074, TAPLFO3, 1N4148, resistors, capacitors, pots) with no package or mounting style (0805, SOIC, DIP, TO-92, THT, SMD) stated anywhere on the page.

lineage.credit: I decided to go in on an Electric Druid TAPLFO3 chip and put the headache behind me.
lineage.source_is: Electric Druid's product page for the TAPLFO3 chip (the LFO IC the module is built around)
lineage.quote: I decided to go in on an Electric Druid TAPLFO3 chip and put the headache behind me.

lineage.credit: Design relies largely on the TAPLFO3 datasheet, with clarification on bipolar pin behavior from Electric Druid support ("Tom")
lineage.quote: Relying largely on the datasheet, with a few tweaks, Liberty Bell 7 is an automation/modulation powerhouse

other_links: https://www.mechlabindustries.com/eurorack-schematics/voltage-daikaiju/ (link to another Mechlab module page, not visited per scope)
notes: No HP/width or licence statement found anywhere on the page. BOM has no package/mounting info, so components left null rather than guessed.
